selection.rationale: The project metric is peak_allocated_bytes for frozen offline batch=32 FP32 NCHW ResNet-18 inference. Signature evidence in calls.json locates the peak-forming execution in the embeddings stage: conv2d consumes (32,3,224,224) (about 19.3 MB persistent pixels) and produces (32,64,112,112) FP32 (about 102.8 MB); the following aten::batch_norm (call 279a256c150755fd69216f5a) allocates a second (32,64,112,112) output while the conv output is still live, and the out-of-place aten::relu (ddf82d5c5c82c55ac9ae09f1) allocates a third equivalent buffer while the BN output is still live. Every later stage operates on tensors of at most (32,128,28,28)/(32,256,14,14)/(32,512,7,7), i.e. about 25.7 MB, so no downstream moment can exceed the roughly 2x102.8 MB of concurrent activations set here (plus about 46.8 MB parameters and 19.3 MB pixels). The selected region is the contiguous ResNetEmbeddings subtree (embedder conv->BN->ReLU plus pooler, groups each verified single-callsite with exactly one call), which is a coherent editable boundary in the project model-preparation/forward path; profiler record_function groups are excluded as instrumentation. The two edits are coupled and must be joint: folding inference BN parameters into the 7x7 conv weights/bias alone still leaves the out-of-place ReLU allocating a second 102.8 MB buffer, and an in-place ReLU alone still leaves the BN input/output pair live; only together does exactly one (32,64,112,112) buffer exist at any instant, with the maxpool moment (102.8 + 25.7 MB) becoming the new floor. Workload, FP32/NCHW policy, TF32-disabled policy and quality checks are untouched; no call reordering or dependency change is proposed. Diagnostic CUDA durations were used only to confirm the region is on the critical path, never summed across the nested ancestor/child families, and the selection is justified by allocation structure rather than local kernel speed, since a faster kernel need not move peak_allocated_bytes.
selection.hypothesis: Collapsing the embeddings conv->BN->ReLU chain to a single live (32,64,112,112) FP32 buffer - by folding the BN running statistics into the 7x7 conv weights and bias once at model preparation (eval mode, running_mean/running_var are fixed) and applying ReLU in place on the conv output - will reduce peak_allocated_bytes by approximately one 102.8 MB activation buffer (roughly 35-40 percent of the activation-driven peak, from about 2x102.8 MB concurrent to about 102.8+25.7 MB at the new maxpool floor), while images_per_second stays at or above 0.95x baseline because the change removes one BN kernel and one full 102.8 MB activation write/read pair (BN and ReLU groups here total about 443 diagnostic us of a 4141 us run) and adds no work, and logits remain within atol=rtol=1e-4 with identical top-1 since folding only reassociates the affine BN math around the conv. This is a hypothesis to be tested by paired measurement on the frozen workload; if the measured peak is instead dominated by cudnn workspace or allocator fragmentation inside conv2d, the expected reduction will not materialize and the selection must be revised.

proposal.rationale: The project metric is peak_allocated_bytes for the frozen offline batch=32 FP32 NCHW ResNet-18 run, and the selection locates the peak in the embeddings stage: the stem 7x7 stride-2 conv allocates a (32,64,112,112) FP32 buffer (~102.8 MB), the following eval-mode aten::batch_norm allocates a second equivalent buffer while the conv output is still live, and the out-of-place aten::relu adds a third transient; every later stage works on tensors of at most ~25.7 MB, so only this stage sets the peak. This candidate implements the selected joint edit as three functional replacements strictly inside the stem ResNetConvLayer (model.resnet.embedder.embedder), declared at exactly the three observed call sites: (1) 220b9d0ec76e2ccc01dcdb09 (aten::conv2d, under module call 8ef2341287e5b4afa9d0e7bf) is reissued with build-time folded weights W' = gamma/sqrt(var+eps) * W and bias b' = beta - gamma*mu/sqrt(var+eps) (the stem conv has bias=None, the BN is eval-mode with fixed running stats and eps=1e-5), which is algebraically identical to BN(conv(x)) up to FP32 reassociation; (2) 279a256c150755fd69216f5a (aten::batch_norm, under 2f3bfb9ee01d701be01d2ff3) becomes an identity passthrough returning its input tensor unchanged when that input provably is the folded conv output, so no second 102.8 MB buffer is allocated; (3) ddf82d5c5c82c55ac9ae09f1 (aten::relu, under 35096a239aa1290aabeed5de) applies relu_ in place on that same buffer and returns it, so the ReLU allocates nothing. After the change exactly one (batch,64,112,112) FP32 buffer is live in the stem, and the new peak moment is the maxpool one (102.8 MB conv output + 25.7 MB pool output) plus the persistent ~46.8 MB parameters and ~19.3 MB pixels, versus two concurrent ~102.8 MB activation buffers at baseline: an expected reduction of roughly one 102.8 MB buffer, about 25-30 percent of the measured peak. Throughput should stay above the 0.95x baseline constraint because the change removes one full 102.8 MB BN read/write pair plus its kernel and one full out-of-place ReLU output write, and adds only a conv bias term on an otherwise identical conv geometry. No observed call is eliminated: the stem modules and all record functions still execute and the framework still observes one dispatch per site; aten::batch_norm is replaced by an identity passthrough call, not removed, so eliminated_calls is empty and the plan needs no recapture. Every replacement guards the observed signature structurally (float32, device match with the module parameter, 4-D input, input channels == conv.in_channels, stride/padding/dilation/groups equal to the Conv2d attributes, bias=None, identity or exact equality of the original weight Parameter, eval mode) and otherwise falls back to the parent operator from context['references']; the folded conv output is tagged (tensor attribute, with an id-keyed fallback if attribute assignment is unavailable), and the BN/relu replacements only take the fused path when their input carries that tag, so any fallback combination (conv folds or not) degrades cleanly to parent behavior and double normalization cannot occur; the tag is cleared at the ReLU and no cross-iteration state survives. Guards are batch-size-agnostic (channel/stride geometry only), so the held-out unseen_batch=7 workload exercises the same fused path rather than silently falling back. Model parameters, BN buffers and running statistics are left untouched (the folded tensors are new invariant parameter-derived constants), so state and alias semantics are preserved and the warm-model lifecycle across reset()/warmup/repeats/continuous steps is unaffected. This is a single-rank task; the mapping is returned for the local rank only and involves no collectives, no extra streams and no synchronization. inputs/previous-feedback.txt does not exist, so this is the first attempt for this selection. CPU verification with the real pretrained weights and the real pixel fixtures (batch 8, held-out 7 and the frozen 32): logits allclose at atol=rtol=1e-4 with exact top-1 (max abs deviation ~6.7e-6), exactly one fused conv, one identity BN and one in-place ReLU per forward, and clean parent fallback for every other BN/ReLU call that reaches the callables (including 64-channel encoder sites).

setup_work.description: During build(), once per prepared state before validation: resolve the physical stem Conv2d/BatchNorm2d from context['modules'] (falling back to a model-tree walk); validate eval mode, track_running_stats, float32 dtypes and shape consistency; compute scale = gamma/sqrt(running_var + eps), folded_weight (64,3,7,7) = W*scale.view(-1,1,1,1) and folded_bias (64,) = beta - mu*scale with two tiny elementwise ops on the model device under torch.no_grad(); probe once whether tensor attribute tagging works (otherwise an id-keyed dict marker is used). No model parameter or buffer is modified, no backend or allocator flag is touched, no synchronization is issued, and nothing is cached that depends on input data.
setup_work.persistent_extra_detail: folded_weight 64*3*7*7*4 = 37632 B + folded_bias 64*4 = 256 B, about 0.04 percent of one saved 102.8 MB activation buffer
setup_work.transient_extra_bytes: on the order of the folded tensors themselves during the two elementwise setup kernels

quality_risks: BN folding reassociates the affine normalization around the conv accumulation in FP32 (TF32 remains disabled), so logits drift by FP32-rounding-scale amounts (measured max ~6.7e-6 absolute on the real fixture batch=32 on CPU) versus the parent; the frozen tolerance is atol=rtol=1e-4 with exact_top1, which the drift does not breach in CPU verification, but exact top-1 remains the sensitive check if two logits were separated by less than the drift; only paired GPU measurement by the framework can confirm this on the bound device.

aten::relu is replaced by an in-place relu_ on the folded conv output. Alias equivalence is established: that buffer is freshly allocated by the fused conv inside the same call, its only consumer is the stem ReLU result (the ResNetConvLayer forward rebinds immediately, the workload runs under inference_mode so there are no autograd version-counter consumers, and no other reference to the tensor exists), so mutating it in place is observationally identical for every external output and state.

conv2d is now issued with a bias tensor where the parent call had bias=None; if the framework's functional dispatch matched operators loosely by signature this could re-dispatch the internal folded call, but the replacement's own guard (weight identity/equality with the original Parameter) terminates any such recursion at the parent operator with the same folded arguments, so results remain correct; the recorded call's bias=None signature also differs from the internal call's bias tensor.

All fallback paths are numerically exact parent behavior; the risk profile is therefore asymmetric: guard failure can lose the memory improvement but cannot corrupt outputs, while the active fused path carries only the reassociation risk described above. If the measured GPU peak is instead dominated by cudnn workspace or allocator fragmentation inside conv2d, the expected one-buffer reduction will not materialize and the proposal must be revised (per the selection hypothesis).

usage.scope: Observed assistant message snapshots; provider estimates, not invoice
Observed assistant message snapshots; provider estimates, not invoice

external_invariants: Model is ResNetForImageClassification loaded from the local assets directory only (local_files_only=True) in float32; no downloads.
All weights and activations remain FP32; torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 and torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 are False and torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest').
Seed policy: torch.manual_seed(20261020) applied in prepare, matching common.configure().

Input is the real preprocessed image fixture tensor from assets/pixels.npy (3 images, NCHW float32), selected as images[torch.arange(batch) % len(images)].contiguous(); for the frozen 'online' workload batch=1, i.e. the first image, unchanged every repeat.
The model is in eval() mode and the forward pass runs under torch.inference_mode(), identical to the source infer() helper calling model(pixel_values=pixels).logits.
Batch size is fixed at 1 for this workload; the workload, data, precision and output requirements are not altered to improve the score.
Correctness requires all logits within atol=1e-4 / rtol=1e-4 and exact top-1 argmax equality against the reference; observations include every logit and the predicted class integer.

Latency is wall time around run() with CUDA synchronization at both boundaries, per the source's per-repeat timing; throughput is derived from the unchanged work amount (batch=1) and the measured elapsed time.
The adapter does not initialize CUDA or load the model at import time and never destroys the process group in reset.
